adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — A non-string backupCode in the JSON body (e.g. a number) makes req.body.backupCode.replaceAll throw an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 validation error.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path checks `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` and then unconditionally calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If the JSON body supplies a truthy non-string (e.g. `123`), `replaceAll` is not a function and the handler will throw, resulting in an unhandled 500 rather than returning a 400. There is no type validation/guard in the diff to ensure `backupCode` is a string before calling `replaceAll`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — Backup codes are shown only after 2FA is already enabled; if the dialog is dismissed through onOpenChange (Esc or overlay) instead of Close, the one-time codes are lost with no way to view them again short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are only rendered in the new `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` step, which is reached only after `handleEnable` succeeds (`setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`), and the codes live only in component state (`backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`). In that step, the UI removes the Cancel button and only offers Close/Copy/Download actions; there is no handling in `onOpenChange` to force copy/download, call `onEnable`, or reset state. However, the claim that dismissing via `onOpenChange` (Esc/overlay) necessarily causes permanent loss of the codes cannot be verified from this diff because the parent component’s `onOpenChange` behavior/unmounting is not shown; the modal could remain mounted and reopen with state intact. So it’s a real, diff-grounded edge-case/UX concern, but not a definitively provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — Unvalidated req.body.backupCode is called with .replaceAll, so a non-string value from any API caller crashes with an unhandled 500 instead of a structured 400 error.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path checks only truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`) and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If an API caller sends a non-string truthy value (e.g., object/number), `.replaceAll` will throw a TypeError. The diff does not show any input type validation or local try/catch to convert this into a structured 400 response, so this can crash the handler and return a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:137 — Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have backupCodes=null and no endpoint to generate them, so the new "lost access" login/disable contract always returns MissingBackupCodes for existing users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a backup-code path for login/disable when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` (next-auth-options.ts) and explicitly errors if `user.backupCodes` is null (`MissingBackupCodes`). Backup codes are only generated/stored in the new `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` endpoint, and the diff shows no backfill/migration logic or separate “generate backup codes for already-enabled 2FA” endpoint/flow. So pre-migration 2FA users without `backupCodes` cannot use the new “lost access” path and will hit `MissingBackupCodes`, but they can still use TOTP; this is a real compatibility/feature-completeness gap rather than a strict correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — Shared PasswordField now sets tabIndex=-1 on the visibility toggle for every consumer app-wide, making it unreachable by keyboard without regard to other callers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `tabIndex={-1}` to the PasswordField visibility-toggle `<button>` (packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx). A negative tabIndex removes the control from the tab order, so keyboard users can no longer reach the toggle via normal navigation. Since PasswordField is shared, this change affects all consumers app-wide and constitutes a functional accessibility regression introduced by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 — Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write, so concurrent logins can reuse the same single-use code (and a concurrent update can resurrect a consumed code)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code use is implemented as: decrypt `user.backupCodes` → `JSON.parse` → find `index` → set `backupCodes[index] = null` → `prisma.user.update` writing the whole re-encrypted array. This is a non-atomic read/modify/write. Two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both read the same pre-consumption value, both pass the `index` check, and both succeed before either update is observed (single-use code can be reused). Additionally, concurrent consumption of different codes can cause a lost update: a later write based on stale decrypted data can overwrite the other update and effectively restore a previously-nullled code ("resurrect" it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — After enable succeeds the modal moves to DisplayBackupCodes, but closing via onOpenChange (Esc/overlay) skips onEnable and resetState, leaving the UI showing 2FA as disabled and the modal stuck on the backup-codes step

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable()` (handleEnable: `if (response.status === 200) { setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); return; }`). The only place that calls `onEnable()` + `resetState()` on that step is the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes footer. However the Dialog is controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange` and the component does not wrap `onOpenChange` to call `resetState()` (or `onEnable()`) when the modal is dismissed via overlay click/Esc. Also, the Cancel button is hidden on `DisplayBackupCodes` (`{step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>{t("cancel")}</Button> : null}`), making overlay/Esc a likely close path. This can leave internal `step` stuck at DisplayBackupCodes on next open, and the parent UI may not update because `onEnable()` was skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 — Backup code matching is case-sensitive against lowercase hex, so codes typed in uppercase are rejected (same in disable.ts:61)

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex via `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (setup.ts) and stored as-is. Matching during login (`next-auth-options.ts`) and 2FA disable (`disable.ts`) compares `backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` directly against stored codes with `indexOf(...)` and does not normalize case. Therefore a user-entered uppercase backup code (a common manual-entry variant) will fail to match and be incorrectly rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — No backfill or regeneration path for existing 2FA users, whose backupCodes stay NULL so backup-code login always fails with MissingBackupCodes until they disable and re-enable 2FA

adjudication.rationale: The migration only adds a nullable `users.backupCodes` column (no backfill). New backup-code flows explicitly error when `backupCodes` is missing (e.g., `next-auth-options.ts` throws `MissingBackupCodes` if `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes`; `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` returns `MissingBackupCodes` when `req.body.backupCode` is present but `!user.backupCodes`). Backup codes are only generated in the 2FA setup endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`), so existing 2FA-enabled users will not have backup codes unless they go through setup again. This is a real, diff-grounded product/edge-case gap rather than a correctness regression in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 — Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write, so concurrent logins can reuse the same code or overwrite each other's updates

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code verification does a read/decrypt (`symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)`), then modifies in-memory (`backupCodes[index] = null`), then writes back with `prisma.user.update(...)`. There is no transactional/conditional update tying the write to the previously-read value, so two concurrent authorize calls can both validate the same `credentials.backupCode` before either update commits, allowing the same backup code to be accepted twice (single-use guarantee violated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 — Backup-code verification (env-key check, decrypt, JSON.parse, dash-strip, indexOf) is copy-pasted from next-auth-options.ts:131-145 instead of a shared helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows near-identical backup-code verification logic implemented in two places: the new block in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (env key check, decrypt + `JSON.parse`, `replaceAll("-", "")`, `indexOf` match) and the added branch in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` for login authorization. This is clear duplication introduced by the PR and creates a maintainability/consistency risk (future fixes could be applied to one path but not the other), but it is not, by itself, a functional defect evidenced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:163 — Backup-code format (10 hex chars, XXXXX-XXXXX) is encoded ad hoc in setup.ts, formatBackupCode, BackupCode.tsx min/maxLength, and two replaceAll("-") calls with no shared constant/helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the backup-code shape is implicitly duplicated in multiple places: generation in `setup.ts` uses `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (10 hex chars), display formatting in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` via `formatBackupCode` slices into `XXXXX-XXXXX`, input constraints in `BackupCode.tsx` (`minLength={10}`, `maxLength={11}`, placeholder), and normalization in two separate server paths using `replaceAll("-", "")` (API disable endpoint and `next-auth-options.ts` authorize). adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:64 — useState([]) is untyped (never[]), so backupCodes loses its string[] type at the API/UI boundary

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx the state is initialized as `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);`, which in TypeScript typically infers `never[]` for an empty array literal. That means `backupCodes` is not typed as `string[]` despite later being treated as a list of strings (e.g. `backupCodes.map((code) => ... formatBackupCode(code) ...)` and `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(...).join("\n"))`). This is a real, diff-grounded type-safety issue (API/UI boundary loses the intended `string[]` typing), though it may not manifest as a runtime bug because `response.json()` is effectively `any`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:31 — DisplayBackupCodes is inserted second in the SetupStep enum though it is the final step, making enum order misrepresent the flow and shifting numeric values

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SetupStep` is a local enum used only within `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` via symbolic members (e.g., `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and `step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`), not by relying on numeric ordering. There’s no evidence in the shown code that enum numeric values are persisted, compared by `<`/`>`, or consumed externally, so inserting `DisplayBackupCodes` second does not verifiably break behavior or misrepresent the flow in any functional way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:121 — Copy test only waits for a success toast without checking clipboard contents, so it passes even if wrong codes are copied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:61 — No test verifies setup generates, encrypts and returns backup codes or that re-running setup rotates them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code generation/storage/return behavior in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` (generates `backupCodes` via `crypto.randomBytes`, stores them encrypted in `user.backupCodes` with `symmetricEncrypt(...)`, and returns them in the JSON response).
